info.title: Capisum API
info.description:
API for creating payouts and querying transactions. Authenticate with an organization API key (`Authorization: Bearer cps_...`). The key's environment (staging or production) scopes provider credentials.

**Shipped today:** Payouts in NGN, GHS, and KES.

get.description: Returns provider slugs Capisum can route to when connected in your workspace. Includes NGN bank payout providers and Quidax crypto wallet payouts.

get.summary: Get payout contract and provider capabilities
get.description: Returns supported payout providers, currencies, countries, destination types, and per-rail `required_fields` for the current contract version. Capabilities are derived from each provider's payout profile (not a hardcoded global currency list). Use each provider's `rails` array to see what Capisum can route for that provider.

Returns Capisum canonical bank identifiers for payouts. Use `bank_id` on payout recipients; Capisum resolves provider-specific codes at execution time. Filter with `provider` to see only banks mappable to that provider and include that provider's `bank_code`.
Returns the latest health snapshot for a provider in the API key's environment. If no health data exists, returns `{ "status": "unknown" }`.

Returns the available balance for a connected provider in the API key's environment. Amounts are in minor units (for example, `500000` = ₦5,000.00 in NGN; Quidax crypto uses 8 decimals). Supported for `fincra`, `paystack`, `flutterwave`, `palmpay`, and `quidax`.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Optional currency or asset filter (e.g. NGN, USDT, BTC).

post.description: Resolve a bank account name through a connected provider that supports account resolution. `provider` is optional: omit it to use the dashboard account default, or enable Override request provider to ignore a sent provider. Use `bank_id` from `GET /v1/reference/banks` when possible. Supported for `fincra`, `paystack`, `flutterwave`, `palmpay`, and `quidax`.

Create a payout through Capisum routing. Amounts are in minor units (for example, `500000` = ₦5,000.00 in NGN; Quidax crypto uses 8 decimals, so `500000000` = 5 USDT).

Capisum accepts one canonical `destination` shape; each provider adapter translates it. Use `GET /v1/payouts/capabilities` for provider-specific currencies, countries, rails, and `required_fields`. Validation depends on the resolved provider + country + currency + rail (USD ACH differs from NGN bank transfer). NGN catalog banks use `GET /v1/reference/banks` for `bank_id`. Crypto wallet payouts use top-level `currency` with `destination.type = crypto_wallet`, `destination.address`, and `destination.network`.

Payouts are queued for asynchronous provider submission. A successful response returns `status: queued` with your merchant `reference`. Capisum assigns per-attempt provider transfer references internally.

Requires `X-Idempotency-Key`.

parameters.name: X-Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique key for safe retries. Reusing a key returns the original transaction.

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
x-codeSamples.source:
curl -X POST https://api.capisum.com/v1/transactions/payout \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer cps_your_key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: payout-order-123" \
  -d '{
    "amount": "500000",
    "currency": "NGN",
    "provider": "fincra",
    "destination": {
      "type": "bank_account",
      "bank_id": "ng.opay",
      "account_number": "7068270185",
      "account_name": "Test Recipient"
    }
  }'

post.description:
Generate a crypto deposit address on the merchant Quidax or Bitnob account. Funds settle to the merchant wallet. Customer is optional Capisum metadata.

Send `asset` (e.g. `usdt`) and `network` (e.g. `trc20`). Amounts are 8-decimal minor units (for example, `500000000` = 5 USDT). The address is returned on `deposit`, with `deposit.wallet` = `merchant_wallet`. Listen for webhooks; `transaction.settled` confirms the deposit.

Requires `X-Idempotency-Key`.

parameters.name: X-Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique key for safe retries. Reusing a key returns the original transaction.

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
x-codeSamples.source:
curl -X POST https://api.capisum.com/v1/transactions/pay-in/merchant-wallet \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer cps_your_key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: payin-merchant-123" \
  -d '{
    "amount": "500000000",
    "asset": "usdt",
    "network": "trc20",
    "provider": "quidax"
  }'

post.description:
Generate a crypto deposit address attributed to `customer.email` (Quidax sub-account or Bitnob customer-linked address). `customer.name` is optional.

Send `asset` (e.g. `usdt`), `network` (e.g. `trc20`), and `customer.email`. Amounts are 8-decimal minor units (for example, `500000000` = 5 USDT). The address is returned on `deposit`, with `deposit.wallet` = `customer_wallet`. Listen for webhooks; `transaction.settled` confirms the deposit.

Requires `X-Idempotency-Key`.

parameters.name: X-Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique key for safe retries. Reusing a key returns the original transaction.

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
x-codeSamples.source:
curl -X POST https://api.capisum.com/v1/transactions/pay-in/customer-wallet \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer cps_your_key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: payin-customer-123" \
  -d '{
    "amount": "500000000",
    "asset": "usdt",
    "network": "trc20",
    "provider": "quidax",
    "customer": {
      "email": "ada@example.com",

get.description: List transactions for your organization. Results are cursor-paginated.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Transaction ID cursor for the next page.

parameters.name: ending_before
parameters.description: Transaction ID cursor for the previous page.

parameters.name: status_group
parameters.description: Filter by lifecycle group. `pending` includes queued/processing states; `review` includes uncertain/manual_review.

post.description: Poll the upstream provider for the latest status and update the transaction record.

Create a Capisum customer, resolve the pay-in provider (dashboard configuration wins over request `provider` when both exist), immediately create the provider customer when the adapter requires one, and return the Capisum customer with selected provider and normalized verification status/requirements. Provider customer IDs stay internal.

Some pay-in providers require `email`, `phone` (E.164), and `country` before they will issue a destination. Supplying them up front avoids a second round trip.

`reference` is your own identifier and is unique per environment — reusing it returns the existing customer instead of creating a duplicate.

get.description: List customers in the API key's environment. Results are cursor-paginated.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Customer ID cursor for the next page.

parameters.name: ending_before
parameters.description: Customer ID cursor for the previous page.

get.description: Read a customer, including the current `verification_status`. While verification is still open, Capisum refreshes status from the provider. Poll this after `POST /v1/customers/{id}/kyc`. `verification_url` is only present as a hosted fallback when the provider exposes one.

post.description:
Submit identity verification for a customer through the pay-in provider's KYC API. Capisum loads the existing ProviderCustomer mapping, translates the provider-neutral payload, submits it to the provider KYC API, and normalizes status to `submitted`, `approved`, `rejected`, or `requires_action`. `provider` / `currency` are optional when the customer was already bound at create time; when both request and dashboard routing exist, dashboard wins.

Pay-in destinations that require provider KYC stay blocked until the provider reports approval (`verification_status: approved` and destination creation allowed).

put.description: Correct or complete a KYC submission after a rejection. Send only the fields that need updating, plus `provider` or `currency` for routing.

post.description:
Create a virtual account where a customer can send fiat. Capisum resolves the provider, creates or reuses the provider's customer record, checks verification, then returns normalized bank account details you can display directly.

`type: bank_account` is the only destination type on this endpoint today. Yativo covers BRL, MXN/MXNBASE, USD/USDBASE, and EUR/EURBASE. Fincra covers NGN (requires `metadata.bvn`), GHS, and KES. Crypto deposit addresses use POST /v1/transactions/pay-in/merchant-wallet or POST /v1/transactions/pay-in/customer-wallet.

When the provider still needs the customer to finish verification, the response returns `status: verification_required`. Submit KYC with `POST /v1/customers/{id}/kyc` (primary), or use `verification_url` only when the provider exposes a hosted fallback, then retry.

Destinations are reusable: repeating the same request for the same customer, provider, type, and currency returns the existing active destination rather than creating another.

get.description: List pay-in destinations, optionally filtered by customer. Results are cursor-paginated.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Destination ID cursor for the next page.

parameters.name: ending_before
parameters.description: Destination ID cursor for the previous page.

get.description: Read a destination and its banking or crypto details. Deposits into this destination create `pay_in` transactions linked to both the destination and its customer.

post.description: Price a fiat-to-crypto on-ramp. Amounts are source-asset minor units (NGN/GHS use 2 decimals; crypto uses 8). Requires `X-Idempotency-Key`. Reuse the same key to refresh an expired quote without creating a duplicate.

parameters.name: X-Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique key for safe retries. Reusing a key returns or refreshes the original quote.

post.description: Start a fiat-to-crypto on-ramp from a quote. Returns payment instructions (bank account or mobile money). Settlement happens asynchronously via webhooks. Requires `X-Idempotency-Key`.

parameters.name: X-Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique key for safe retries. Reusing a key returns the original transaction.

get.description: Poll the provider and return the latest Capisum status. Does not mark completion from provider acceptance alone.

post.description: Confirm a GHS mobile-money OTP after initiating an on-ramp with payment.type = mobile_money.
Price a crypto-to-fiat off-ramp. Amounts are source-asset minor units. Requires `X-Idempotency-Key`.
Start a crypto-to-fiat off-ramp from a quote. Returns a crypto deposit address. Fiat payout completes asynchronously. Requires `X-Idempotency-Key`.
Price an asset-to-asset conversion with no bank collection or payout. Requires `X-Idempotency-Key`.
Execute a conversion quote. Status remains processing until the provider settles. Requires `X-Idempotency-Key`.

apiKeyAuth.description: Organization API key (`cps_...`) from the Capisum dashboard.

provider.description: Connected provider slug (for example, `palmpay` or `paystack`). Optional: when omitted, Capisum uses the dashboard account default. When Override request provider is enabled, this field is ignored.

bank_id.description: Capisum canonical bank id from GET /v1/reference/banks (recommended).

bank_code.description: Optional provider-specific bank code escape hatch when bank_id is unavailable.

ledger.description: Total wallet balance in minor units when the provider exposes it.

PayoutBankDestination.description: Bank / local rail destination. Required fields depend on the resolved provider rail (see GET /v1/payouts/capabilities → providers[].rails[].required_fields).

account_number.description: Bank account number, CLABE, CCI, or similar local account identifier.

bank_id.description: Capisum canonical bank id from GET /v1/reference/banks (e.g. ng.opay). Required for many NGN rails.

bank_code.description: Corridor bank code when Capisum bank_id is not used.

name.description: Beneficiary legal / full name. Falls back to account_name when omitted.

physical_address.description: Beneficiary street address for provider beneficiary APIs.

network.description: Quidax blockchain network (for example, trc20, erc20, bep20, bitcoin).

destination_tag.description: Optional memo/tag for networks that require it.

mobile_money_code.description: Normalized network label. GHS: MTN, AIRTEL. KES: SAFARICOM, AIRTEL.

MerchantWalletPayInRequest.description: Merchant wallet pay-in. The deposit address is created on the merchant Quidax or Bitnob account.

amount.description: Amount in 8-decimal minor units for crypto (500000000 = 5 USDT).

asset.description: Crypto asset ticker (e.g. btc, usdt). Alias for currency.

network.description: Quidax blockchain network (e.g. trc20, erc20, bep20, bitcoin).

customer.description: Optional Capisum customer record. Not sent to Quidax for merchant-wallet pay-ins.

CustomerWalletPayInRequest.description: Customer wallet pay-in. The deposit address is attributed to customer.email (Quidax sub-account or Bitnob customer address).

amount.description: Amount in 8-decimal minor units for crypto (500000000 = 5 USDT).

asset.description: Crypto asset ticker (e.g. btc, usdt). Alias for currency.

network.description: Quidax blockchain network (e.g. trc20, erc20, bep20, bitcoin).

customer.description: Identifies the Quidax sub-account. Email is unique and immutable; name is optional and mapped to first/last name.

amount.description: Amount in minor units. Quidax crypto uses 8 decimal places (500000000 = 5 USDT).

reference.description: Optional merchant-facing payout reference (16–50 chars; lowercase letters, digits, `_`, `-`). Capisum generates a provider-safe `pout_*` reference when omitted.

countries.description: Present when more than one country appears across provider rails for this currency.

required_fields.description: Capisum destination fields required for this rail.

bank_code.description: Provider bank code when `provider` is set; otherwise the CBN code for NGN banks.

provider.description: Provider slug used to filter banks and select bank_code. Null when unfiltered.

customer_id.description: Customer this transaction belongs to, when one is known.

pay_in_destination_id.description: Pay-in destination the money arrived in, for `pay_in` transactions.

deposit.description: Crypto deposit address details for Quidax pay-ins.

authorization_url.description: Present on pay-in create responses when the provider returns a checkout URL.

wallet.description: merchant_wallet settles to the merchant Quidax account. customer_wallet settles to a per-customer sub-account.

message.example: The selected provider is not supported.

phone.description: E.164 format. Required by some pay-in providers.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3. Required by some pay-in providers.

provider.description: Preferred pay-in provider. Ignored when the dashboard already has a matching pay_in route for `currency` (dashboard configuration wins).

currency.description: Used with dashboard routing defaults to resolve the pay-in provider.

reference.description: Your own identifier. Unique per environment; reusing it returns the existing customer.

provider.description: Selected pay-in provider slug. Never a provider customer ID.

verification_url.description: Optional hosted verification fallback. Direct KYC via POST /v1/customers/{id}/kyc is the primary flow.

due.description: Provider-reported outstanding verification items, when available.

CustomerKycRequest.description: Provider-neutral KYC/KYB payload. Capisum maps fields onto the selected provider's documented API. `provider` / `currency` are optional when the customer already has a ProviderCustomer binding from create; dashboard routing wins when both exist.

CustomerKycUpdateRequest.description: Partial KYC correction fields plus `provider` or `currency` for routing.

provider.description: Optional. Omit to let Capisum routing rules choose a pay-in provider.

PayInDestinationDetails.description: Only the fields the provider returned are present.

PayInDestinationVerificationRequired.description: Returned instead of a destination when the provider still needs the customer to complete verification. Submit KYC via POST /v1/customers/{id}/kyc. `verification_url` is only a hosted fallback when the provider exposes one.
